title: Adaptive histogram thresholds for embedding quant profiles and cosine drift detection
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: We need a robust calibration and validation workflow for embedding model quantization (INT8 and FP16 profiles) that minimizes similarity regressions in production. Current calibration runs use fixed per-layer clipping scales and global thresholds; those settings do not adapt well to corpus shifts and lead to cosine-similarity drifts on long-tail datasets. This ticket designs and implements an adaptive histogram-threshold based quantization profile generation flow plus an operational cosine drift detector and rollback gating for embed-serving routes.

Goals:
- Produce INT8 and FP16-compatible quantization profiles for embedding models that preserve cosine similarity for a representative set of production corpora (docs, queries, code-snippets).
- Implement adaptive histogram-based scale selection per-tensor (instead of fixed percentiles) to reduce outlier sensitivity.
- Add a continuous cosine-similarity drift detector with multi-window baselines (hour, day, week) and alerting thresholds tied to a per-corpus baseline.
- Wire gating so that if a quantized profile causes a similarity regression above tolerance, traffic automatically falls back to the last known-good float/FP16 variant and opens a rollback PR.

Scope: calibration pipeline code (offline), profile artifact format updates, evaluation harness changes, monitoring dashboards, alert rules, and runbook updates. Excludes full re-training or model architecture changes.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline can generate INT8 and FP16 profile artifacts with per-tensor adaptive scales stored in the new v2 profile schema.
Evaluation harness computes cosine similarity distributions for reference vs quantized embeddings and emits a summary report (mean, p50, p95, fraction below threshold) per corpus.
Drift detector runs continuously and creates an alert when short-window similarity drops > 3% relative and absolute p95 drops below 0.78 for any critical corpus (configurable).
Automatic rollback policy triggers for deploys where the quantized profile causes > 0.5% of queries to fall under the degradation floor, with an audit entry and PR template created.
Grafana dashboard updated with new panels: per-corpus similarity histogram, rolling mean, alert annotations; runbook entry added with step-by-step remediation.
Documentation: Confluence doc describing algorithm, config knobs, and suggested sampling sizes; example Jupyter notebook for offline validation.
steps: Design adaptive histogram algorithm: choose binning strategy, outlier trimming, and smoothing; produce pseudocode and complexity notes.
Update calibration harness to accept sample shards by corpus and to compute per-tensor histograms for activations and weights.
Implement profile generator that converts histograms into scale/zero-point pairs for INT8 and scale-only for FP16; add serialization to profile-v2.json.
Extend evaluation harness to compute cosine similarity across large sample sets, and to produce per-corpus shard reports and delta-from-float summaries.
Integrate drift detector service: baseline computation, multi-window comparison, anomaly scoring, and webhook alerts to PagerDuty/Slack channel.
Add automated gating in rollout pipeline: dry-run compare, threshold check, fallback wiring in Redwood serving edge, and audit logging.
Create dashboards, alert rules, and a short runbook with playbook steps for SRE and model-ops.
Run end-to-end validation on three representative customers/corpora (internal synthetic, customer-A docs, customer-B codebase).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Adaptive histogram may overfit to the calibration sample and miss rare but important query types. Mitigation: enforce minimum sample diversity and holdout validation corpus, and run stratified sampling by intent/label.

Risk: Increased calibration runtime due to histogram computation on large shards. Mitigation: use streaming histograms with fixed memory footprint and shard-level downsampling; schedule heavy runs during off-peak hours.
Risk: False positives from short-window noise. Mitigation: require multi-window confirmation (e.g., 15m + 6h + 24h) before auto-rollback; provide manual override in console.
Risk: Backwards compatibility with older profile consumers. Mitigation: profile-v2 feature-flagged; runtime will fallback to v1 logic if v2 parsing fails.
Risk: Customer trust erosion if rollback triggers too often. Mitigation: conservative alert thresholds for customer-facing routes and staged rollout defaults.

rollout_plan: Step 1: Merge calibration and profile-v2 support behind feature flag in runtime (canary=false).
Step 2: Run offline generation for 3 models and store artifacts; run evaluation harness and confirm acceptance criteria on holdout corpora.
Step 3: Enable canary deploy for 1% traffic on non-critical customer routes with enhanced logging and telemetry retention.
Step 4: Monitor drift detector for 7 days; if no alerts, increase to 10% for 72 hours, then 50% for 48 hours.
Step 5: If thresholds breached at any stage, trigger auto-rollback and open incident ticket linking evaluation report and samples.
test_plan: Unit tests for histogram streaming edge cases and serialization compatibility.
Integration test: end-to-end generation -> runtime load -> eval harness similarity comparison against float baseline.
Load test: calibration job at scale across 10 shards to measure CPU/memory and runtime overhead.
Canary monitoring: compare production similarity metrics vs canary cohort; automated alerts on regressions.
notes: We will reuse existing embedding eval infra but add corpus tagging to better segment results.
Consider future work: integrate temperature-aware quantization for retrieval models and per-corpus quant profiles pinned at customer level.
Keep profile-v2 schema compact to avoid increasing artifact size; store detailed histograms in archival bucket for audits.
